subtitle: The Apgar checks individual trades. Pre-session readiness checks YOU. Tired, drunk, stressed, in drawdown? Don't trade. Red/yellow/green system that takes 30 seconds and prevents account-killing sessions.

blocks.content:
Some of the biggest losses traders take are not from bad analysis — they're from being in a STATE where good analysis can't be executed properly. Trading tired, drunk, after a fight with your partner, in the middle of a major personal stressor: predictable disaster.

Pre-session readiness is a 30-second check on YOUR CURRENT STATE before you start trading. If you're not green, you don't trade. This single check prevents weeks of recoverable losses turning into account-killing disasters.

blocks.alt: Pre-session readiness traffic-light grid: Sleep / Mood / Recent P&L / Preparation, each with green/yellow/red criteria
blocks.caption: Four-dimension check. ALL GREEN = full trading. Mixed = reduced mode. ANY RED = no trading today.

rows: Under 5 hours, exhausted or hung over
Within normal range; not in drawdown
Down 5%+ from peak; on tilt risk
Reviewed setups + macro context; have a plan

blocks.title: Overall assessment
blocks.content:
• All four GREEN: Full trading mode. Normal sizing. Take A+ setups when they appear.
  • Mixed (greens + yellows): Reduced trading mode. Half normal sizing. Only A+ setups with multiple confluences. Skip B-grade setups.
  • Any RED: NO trading today. Stay flat or close existing positions to safer state. Tomorrow is another day.

The 'any red = no trade' rule is non-negotiable. A red dimension is a warning that decision-making is compromised. Even one red doubles your odds of making expensive mistakes that day.

Sleep deprivation impairs decision-making more than most people realize. Less than 5 hours of sleep produces decision quality similar to legal alcohol intoxication. Trading on insufficient sleep is essentially trading drunk.

  • 7+ hours: full cognitive capacity. Best for active trading.
  • 5-7 hours: somewhat impaired but functional for monitoring positions. Avoid taking new trades.
  • Under 5 hours: RED. Don't open new positions. Existing positions can be monitored but consider taking partial profits to reduce exposure.

This applies whether the cause is genuine insomnia, late-night entertainment, or a baby crying. The cause doesn't matter — the cognitive state does.

Mood affects every decision you make at the screen. Hard rules:

  • Angry: don't trade. Anger increases risk-taking and aggression. Wait for it to fade (often hours).
  • Anxious: don't trade. Anxiety makes you exit winners early and hold losers hoping for recovery. Both destroy edge.
  • Depressed: don't trade. Low motivation often pairs with poor risk-reward decisions.
  • Just had a heated argument: wait 1-2 hours minimum before any trading decisions.
  • Excited about a recent unrelated event: euphoria can also impair judgment. Wait until baseline returns.

The baseline check: 'Am I calm enough to follow my plan if a setup forms in the wrong direction from what I'd prefer?' If the answer is no, stay flat.
Recent P&L — the drawdown danger zone

Drawdowns trigger predictable psychological responses that compound losses if you keep trading through them. The hard rules:

  • Within 0-3% drawdown from peak: GREEN. Continue normally.
  • 3-5% drawdown: YELLOW. Reduce size; take only A+ setups; consider a half-day break.
  • 5%+ drawdown: RED. Stop trading for the day. Re-evaluate strategy. Consider stepping back to small-size or paper for re-validation (lesson 10).
  • 2x normal loss in single trade: RED. Hard daily stop activated.

The discipline of stopping at 3-5% drawdown prevents the 5% from becoming a 25% loss. Most account-killing days started as 'just one more trade to recover'.

blocks.title: The hardest 'red' to enforce: post-loss session
blocks.content:
You're down 5% on the day. Every fiber wants to find another setup to recover. The discipline to STOP is exactly when it's hardest.

Practical aid: have a hard rule pre-committed BEFORE the session starts. 'If I'm down 3%, I close the platform until tomorrow.' Make it physical — close the laptop, walk outside. The friction of re-opening the platform is enough discipline assistance to actually stop.
Preparation — knowing what you're looking for

Trading without prep = trading blind. Pre-session prep should include:

  • HTF context check: where is BTC structurally? What's the 1D/4H trend? Major S/R levels?
  • Macro check: DXY, VIX, ES status. Any major events today?
  • Setup ideas: identify 2-4 specific setups you'd take today. Define entry, SL, TP for each.
  • Risk capacity: how much risk can I deploy today given current drawdown?
  • Schedule: when are you trading? When stopping? Any external commitments?

5-10 minutes of prep makes the difference between trading with a plan and chasing whatever screams loudest on the chart.

Day A — Trading green light

  • Sleep: 7.5 hours, rested → GREEN
  • Mood: calm, just had coffee, focused → GREEN
  • Recent P&L: +1% on the week, +0.5% today → GREEN
  • Preparation: did 10-min review, identified 3 setups, know my macro context → GREEN
  • 4 greens → full trading mode

Day B — Mixed

  • Sleep: 6 hours (woke up early for meeting) → YELLOW
  • Mood: stressed about deadline but functional → YELLOW
  • P&L: flat → GREEN
  • Preparation: quick review, 2 setups identified → GREEN
  • 2 yellows + 2 greens → reduced sizing mode, only A+ setups

Day C — Don't trade

  • Sleep: 4 hours (insomnia) → RED
  • Mood: anxious about sleep loss → YELLOW
  • P&L: down 4% from peak → YELLOW
  • Preparation: none, just opened the screen → RED
  • Any red → NO TRADING TODAY

blocks.title: Take this with you
blocks.content:
Three rules:

  1. Check 4 dimensions before each session: sleep, mood, recent P&L, preparation. 30 seconds.
  2. Traffic light: All green = full trade mode. Mixed = reduced. Any red = NO TRADING.
  3. The 'any red' rule is non-negotiable. One compromised dimension doubles your odds of expensive mistakes that day.
